- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply a 1–3 day lag correction by smoothing out the peak.  
- If true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–4 days post-spike.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (first 5–7 days); apply a 0.5–1% downward bias to first 5 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → -0.33 → 0.67), model may misalign with sentiment cycles; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
